global_rules.title: Total IgE is not diagnostic and does not indicate severity
global_rules.statement: Never present total IgE as proof of allergy, as a severity marker, or as a way to find the trigger. Interpret only against the reference interval printed by the laboratory.
global_rules.enforcement: Block any text that links a total IgE value to severity or diagnosis.

global_rules.title: Specific IgE shows sensitization, not proven allergy
global_rules.statement: Always describe a positive specific IgE as sensitization. Never write that the person is allergic or has an allergy unless a clinician has confirmed it (context flag clinician_confirmed_food_allergy).
global_rules.enforcement: Validator rejects patient text that states allergy as established fact.

global_rules.title: IgE class or value is not severity
global_rules.statement: Show the laboratory class or value as reported. Never convert a class, value or colour into mild, moderate or severe, and never rank allergens by severity.
global_rules.enforcement: Ordering by value is for display only and must not be described as risk.

global_rules.title: No universal positivity cutoff
global_rules.statement: Do not apply a fixed cutoff such as 0.35 kU/L to every allergen. Positive and negative flags, classes and reference limits come from the laboratory report for each test. If the report gives no flag, the status is indeterminate.
global_rules.enforcement: The KB stores no numeric thresholds. Section Builder must read the flag from the Normalizer.

global_rules.title: A negative result is not proof of safety
global_rules.statement: Never write that a negative or low result makes a food, medicine, insect or animal safe. Allergy can exist with a negative blood test.
global_rules.enforcement: Applies to all categories, and is strictest for drugs.

global_rules.title: Do not advise eliminating a tolerated food on IgE alone
global_rules.statement: Never recommend avoiding a food the person eats without symptoms because of a positive IgE. Advise discussing with a doctor. Avoidance advice is allowed only when the clinician has confirmed food allergy (context flag clinician_confirmed_food_allergy).
global_rules.enforcement: Recommendation library carries no avoidance advice for food without that flag.

global_rules.title: No home food challenges after a serious history
global_rules.statement: Never suggest trying or re-trying a food at home. Food challenges are done only under medical supervision. When history_of_serious_reaction is present, the supervised challenge recommendation is excluded.
global_rules.enforcement: food_supervised_challenge is excluded when history_of_serious_reaction is true.

global_rules.title: Drug allergy rules are stricter
global_rules.statement: Do not assume a validated assay exists for any drug. A negative result never means a drug is safe. Never advise starting, stopping, switching or retrying a medicine. Refer to a doctor or drug allergy specialist.
global_rules.enforcement: Every drug record carries C_DRUG and C_DRUG_ROUTE, and the drug recommendations avoid directive medicine advice.

global_rules.title: Insect nuances
global_rules.statement: Venom sensitization shows risk of a sting reaction only in the context of a history. Cockroach and mite results commonly co-occur. Do not give venom immunotherapy advice. Escalate only on a body wide sting reaction history.
global_rules.enforcement: Emergency text appears only with history_of_serious_reaction or sting_reaction_beyond_local.

global_rules.title: Parasite nuances
global_rules.statement: IgE to a parasite does not confirm current infection. Never advise self treatment with worm medicines. Anisakis can also cause true food allergy.

global_rules.title: Occupational and contact nuances
global_rules.statement: Occupational materials matter when exposure is present. Contact skin reactions (for example to henna) are often not IgE mediated, so a blood test cannot decide them. Refer to occupational health or a dermatologist.
global_rules.enforcement: Occupational recommendations require occupational_exposure unless they are product advice (latex).

global_rules.title: Emergency guidance only when history suggests anaphylaxis
global_rules.statement: Show emergency warning signs only when the person reports a serious reaction (history_of_serious_reaction) or a body wide sting reaction. Do not add alarm to routine sensitization findings.

global_rules.title: Missing, invalid or indeterminate results are not negative
global_rules.statement: A test with no value, an invalid value or an indeterminate flag must never be shown as negative, normal or clear.

global_rules.title: Never label a category normal if any test in it is positive
global_rules.statement: Category status uses the words defined in category_status_rules. The word Normal is not used for allergen categories at all.
global_rules.enforcement: Validator rejects the word Normal in allergen category status.

global_rules.title: Unverified claims stay out of patient text
global_rules.statement: Cross reactivity notes and other claims whose evidence status contains pending or unverified are held in the clinical review queue and are not shown to patients.
global_rules.enforcement: patient_note is null in these cases.

global_rules.title: No medical approval is claimed
global_rules.statement: All content is marked pending clinical review. Do not describe it as medically approved or clinically validated until a qualified clinician signs it off.
global_rules.enforcement: clinical_review_status stays pending until sign off.

result_states.positive: The laboratory flagged the result as positive or above its own reporting threshold for this test.
result_states.negative_per_lab: The laboratory reported the result as negative or below its own threshold. This is never shown as safe or normal.
result_states.indeterminate: The result is borderline, flagged as equivocal, or the flag is missing. It is not negative.
result_states.invalid: The value could not be parsed or is out of range. It is not negative.
result_states.missing: The test was ordered but no result is present. It is not negative.

sensitization_detected.label: Sensitization detected
sensitization_detected.when: at least one test in the category is positive
sensitization_detected.note: Never combine with any wording that implies normal.

no_sensitization_detected.label: No sensitization detected
no_sensitization_detected.when: every test in the category has a valid result and all are negative_per_lab
no_sensitization_detected.note: This does not mean allergy is ruled out.

incomplete.label: Results incomplete
incomplete.when: no test is positive and at least one test is indeterminate, invalid or missing
incomplete.note: Shown instead of any reassuring label.

not_tested.label: Not tested
not_tested.when: no test in the category is present in the report
not_tested.note: The category is omitted from Page 3 or shown as not tested.

status_derivation.input: Normalizer supplies per test: value, unit, laboratory class, laboratory flag, laboratory reference or threshold.
status_derivation.positive_source: laboratory flag or class supplied with the report. The KB does not define a numeric threshold.
status_derivation.category_rollup: See category_status_rules. positive in any member overrides everything else. The word Normal is never used for allergen categories.

class_presentation.show: laboratory class and value exactly as reported
never: map class to mild, moderate or severe
class_presentation.ordering_for_display: Order positives by laboratory value only for readability. Do not describe the order as importance.

continuation_rules.many_positives: If more than five tests in one category are positive, list all in the breakdown but show one summary sentence, not one card each.
continuation_rules.cross_reactivity_pairs: When both tests of a cross reactivity pair are positive and the note is shown_to_patient, show the note once for the pair.
continuation_rules.context_missing: If a context flag is unknown treat it as false. Never infer a flag from a result value.

context_vocabulary.reported_symptoms_after_exposure: Person reports symptoms that follow exposure to the allergen or setting.
context_vocabulary.history_of_serious_reaction: Person reports breathing trouble, throat or face swelling, collapse or similar after exposure. Gates emergency text and excludes supervised challenge advice.
context_vocabulary.keeps_or_contacts_animals: Person keeps or regularly handles animals or birds.
context_vocabulary.occupational_exposure: Person handles the material at work or in a hobby.
context_vocabulary.reported_drug_reaction_history: Person reports a past reaction to a medicine.
context_vocabulary.sting_reaction_beyond_local: Person reports a body wide reaction to an insect sting.
context_vocabulary.oral_itching_with_raw_produce: Person reports mouth or throat itching with raw fruit, vegetables or nuts.
context_vocabulary.delayed_symptoms_after_red_meat: Person reports symptoms several hours after eating red meat.
context_vocabulary.clinician_confirmed_food_allergy: A clinician has confirmed a food allergy. The only flag that allows avoidance wording for that food.

C_SENS.patient_text: A positive blood test shows your immune system has made IgE to this substance. This is called sensitization. It does not prove that the substance is causing your symptoms.

C_CLASS.patient_text: The class or value on your report shows how much IgE was found. It does not show how severe a reaction could be, and a higher value does not mean a worse reaction.

C_NEG.patient_text: A negative or low result does not rule out an allergy, and it does not make something safe. Your history and your doctor's advice matter more than this test alone.

C_TOTAL.patient_text: Total IgE is a general marker. It cannot confirm allergy, cannot show which substance you react to, and cannot show how severe any allergy might be.

C_ANIMAL.patient_text: A positive result may involve proteins that several animals share. It does not show that your own pet is the cause, so speak to an allergist before any decision about a pet.

C_BIRD.patient_text: Feathers, droppings and bird products can contain different proteins. A positive result for one bird part does not show which bird or which part matters for you.

C_MITE.patient_text: Dust mite, storage mite and cockroach results often appear together, and they share a protein with shellfish. A positive result does not show which source is responsible.

C_MIXED.patient_text: This test uses a mixture of materials. The result cannot say which part you react to, so it is less specific than a test for a single source.

C_OCC.patient_text: These materials matter most if you touch or breathe them at work or during a hobby. A blood test alone cannot show whether your work is causing symptoms.

C_VENOM.patient_text: A positive venom result shows sensitization and does not prove you will react to the next sting. Anyone with a body wide reaction to a sting should see an allergist.

C_INSECT_XR.patient_text: Cockroach results often appear together with dust mite results, so the true source can be hard to tell apart without your doctor's review.

C_INSECT_OTHER.patient_text: Blood tests for mosquito, housefly and moth have limited published support. A positive result alone does not explain your symptoms, so discuss it with your doctor.

C_POLLEN.patient_text: Pollen results show sensitization. They matter most if nose, eye or chest symptoms follow the local pollen season. Pollen results can overlap with each other.

C_MOULD.patient_text: Mould results show sensitization. Several moulds can share proteins, so one positive result may reflect another mould. Symptoms in damp seasons or damp rooms are useful clues.

C_YEAST.patient_text: Candida lives on normal skin and in the gut, so a positive result often does not mean an infection or a current problem. Your doctor will read it with your symptoms.

C_DRUG.patient_text: Blood IgE tests are not validated for most medicines, and a negative result never means a medicine is safe. Never start, stop or retry a medicine because of this report.

C_DRUG_ROUTE.patient_text: Many medicine reactions do not involve IgE, and some appear days later. A drug allergy specialist decides what testing or supervised steps are right for you.

C_FOOD.patient_text: A positive food result does not mean you must avoid that food. Do not remove foods you eat without symptoms because of this test alone. Your doctor decides with your history.

C_FOOD_LOWER_PERF.patient_text: Blood tests for this food type are less reliable and are often positive in people who eat these foods without trouble. Your history matters far more than this result.

C_PARASITE.patient_text: IgE to worm proteins may reflect past or present exposure and cannot tell which. Never take worm medicines because of this report, and let your doctor decide on further tests.

C_ANISAKIS.patient_text: Anisakis can cause both infection and allergy after eating infected fish. Tell your doctor about hives, swelling or stomach pain after fish meals, especially raw or lightly cooked fish.

steps: Collect positive allergen ids and their canonical categories from derived statuses.
Candidates are recommendations whose applicable_categories include a positive category or whose applicable_allergen_ids include a positive allergen.
Drop candidates whose required_context are not all true or whose exclusions are any true.
Sort by clinical_priority (safety_critical, important, routine), then specific before general, then display_priority, then id.
Keep the first per theme (theme is the dedupe key).
Allow at most one general (gen_) card.
Take up to four. Do not pad.
